rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- distinct customers
customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
-- global month range
range_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    date(min(txn_date),'start of month') AS start_month,
    date(max(txn_date),'start of month') AS end_month
  FROM customer_transactions
),
-- all months between min and max (inclusive)
months AS (
  SELECT start_month AS month_start FROM range_bounds
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date(month_start, '+1 month') FROM months, range_bounds WHERE date(month_start, '+1 month') <= range_bounds.end_month
),
-- cartesian product of customers x months to ensure months with no activity are present
customer_months AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, m.month_start
  FROM customers c CROSS JOIN months m
),
-- closing balance for each customer at end of each month (sum of txn_amount up to last day of that month)
closing_balances AS (
  SELECT
    cm.customer_id,
    cm.month_start,
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(ct.txn_amount)
      FROM customer_transactions ct
      WHERE ct.customer_id = cm.customer_id
        AND date(ct.txn_date) <= date(cm.month_start, '+1 month', '-1 day')
    ), 0) AS closing_balance_for_month
  FROM customer_months cm
)
SELECT
  cb.customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', cb.month_start) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', cb.month_start) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  strftime('%Y-%m', cb.month_start) AS month_key,
  cb.closing_balance_for_month,
  -- monthly change vs previous month (NULL if no previous month)
  CASE
    WHEN LAG(cb.closing_balance_for_month) OVER (PARTITION BY cb.customer_id ORDER BY cb.month_start) IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE cb.closing_balance_for_month - LAG(cb.closing_balance_for_month) OVER (PARTITION BY cb.customer_id ORDER BY cb.month_start)
  END AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative balance through month is the same as closing_balance_for_month (since we treat txn_amount as net change)
  cb.closing_balance_for_month AS cumulative_balance_through_month
FROM closing_balances cb
ORDER BY cb.customer_id, cb.month_start

rows.question: Please help me identify the top 3 bowlers who, in the overs where the maximum runs were conceded in each match, gave up the highest number of runs in a single over across all matches. For each of these bowlers, provide the match in which they conceded these maximum runs. Only consider overs that had the most runs conceded within their respective matches, and among these, determine which bowlers conceded the most runs in a single over overall.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH over_runs AS (
  SELECT
    ob.match_id AS match_id,
    ob.over_id AS over_id,
    ob.bowler AS bowler,
    SUM(bs.runs_scored + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS runs_conceded_in_over
  FROM ball_by_ball ob
  JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON ob.match_id = bs.match_id
   AND ob.over_id = bs.over_id
   AND ob.ball_id = bs.ball_id
   AND ob.innings_no = bs.innings_no
  LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
    ON ob.match_id = er.match_id
   AND ob.over_id = er.over_id
   AND ob.ball_id = er.ball_id
   AND ob.innings_no = er.innings_no
  GROUP BY ob.match_id, ob.over_id, ob.bowler
),
match_max_over AS (
  SELECT
    orun.match_id AS match_id,
    MAX(orun.runs_conceded_in_over) AS match_max_over_runs
  FROM over_runs orun
  GROUP BY orun.match_id
),
-- overs that are the maximum for their match
match_max_overs AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM over_runs o
  JOIN match_max_over m
    ON o.match_id = m.match_id
   AND o.runs_conceded_in_over = m.match_max_over_runs
),
-- for each bowler pick their single best over among these (tie-break by smallest match_id)
bowler_best AS (
  SELECT
    mm.bowler,
    mm.match_id,
    mm.runs_conceded_in_over
  FROM match_max_overs mm
  JOIN (
    SELECT
      bowler,
      MAX(runs_conceded_in_over) AS max_runs
    FROM match_max_overs
    GROUP BY bowler
  ) bmax
    ON mm.bowler = bmax.bowler
   AND mm.runs_conceded_in_over = bmax.max_runs
  -- tie-break: pick smallest match_id if multiple
  GROUP BY mm.bowler
  HAVING mm.match_id = MIN(mm.match_id)
)
SELECT
  p.player_name AS bowler,
  bb.match_id AS match,
  bb.runs_conceded_in_over,
  mmo.match_max_over_runs
FROM bowler_best bb
JOIN player p
  ON bb.bowler = p.player_id
JOIN match_max_over mmo
  ON bb.match_id = mmo.match_id
ORDER BY bb.runs_conceded_in_over DESC, bb.match_id ASC
LIMIT 3

rows.question: Please examine our database records for Chinese cities (country_code_2 = 'cn') during July 2021 and identify both the shortest and longest streaks of consecutive date entries. For each date in these streaks, return exactly one record per date along with the corresponding city name. In your output, please ensure the first letter of each city name is capitalized and the rest are lowercase. Display the dates and city names for both the shortest and longest consecutive date streaks, ordered by date.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- use the actual dates present per hints: 2021-04-01 .. 2021-07-21
dates_in_range AS (
  SELECT date
  FROM legislation_date_dim
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2021-04-01' AND '2021-07-21'
),
-- join dates to Chinese cities on matching insert_date
cn_city_dates AS (
  SELECT
    d.date,
    c.city_id,
    c.city_name
  FROM dates_in_range d
  JOIN cities c
    ON c.insert_date = d.date
  WHERE c.country_code_2 = 'cn'
),
-- numeric date for gap detection (YYYYMMDD)
date_num AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    CAST(replace(date,'-','') AS INTEGER) AS dn
  FROM dates_in_range
),
-- distinct dates for CN cities with numeric value and row number
ordered_dates AS (
  SELECT
    d.date,
    dn.dn,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY dn.dn) AS rn
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT date
    FROM cn_city_dates
  ) d
  JOIN date_num dn ON dn.date = d.date
),
-- groups via (dn - rn)
groups AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    dn,
    rn,
    (dn - rn) AS grp
  FROM ordered_dates
),
-- compute streaks
streaks AS (
  SELECT
    grp,
    MIN(date) AS start_date,
    MAX(date) AS end_date,
    COUNT(*) AS length
  FROM groups
  GROUP BY grp
),
-- find global min and max streak lengths
min_max AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(length) AS min_len,
    MAX(length) AS max_len
  FROM streaks
),
-- target streaks that are either shortest or longest
target_streaks AS (
  SELECT
    s.*,
    CASE WHEN s.length = m.min_len THEN 'shortest' ELSE 'longest' END AS streak_type
  FROM streaks s
  JOIN min_max m
    ON s.length IN (m.min_len, m.max_len)
),
-- expand target streaks into their member dates
streak_dates AS (
  SELECT
    ts.streak_type,
    g.date
  FROM target_streaks ts
  JOIN groups g
    ON g.grp = ts.grp
)
-- final: for each date in selected streaks, return exactly one city and formatted city name
SELECT
  sd.date AS date,
  (UPPER(SUBSTR(c.city_name,1,1)) || LOWER(SUBSTR(c.city_name,2))) AS city_name,
  sd.streak_type
FROM streak_dates sd
JOIN (
  -- pick one deterministic city per date using smallest city_id
  SELECT
    date,
    city_id,
    city_name
  FROM (
    SELECT
      date,
      city_id,
      city_name,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY city_id) AS rn
    FROM cn_city_dates
  ) t
  WHERE rn = 1
) c ON c.date = sd.date
ORDER BY
  CASE sd.streak_type WHEN 'shortest' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
  sd.date

rows.question: Considering all races where pit stop data is available, and focusing on instances when a driver was not behind another car on the previous lap but is behind on the current lap (accounting for retirements, pit-stop entries, pit-stop exits, and race starts), how many times has each type of overtake occurred in Formula 1?

WITH chunk_view_0 AS (
  SELECT
    lp.race_id,
    lp.driver_id,
    lp.lap,
    lp.position AS position_on_lap,
    lp.lap_type,
    lp_prev.position AS prev_position,
    lp_prev.lap AS prev_lap,
    ps.stop AS pit_stop_number,
    ps.lap AS pit_lap,
    ps.time AS pit_time,
    ps.milliseconds AS pit_milliseconds,
    ps.duration AS pit_duration,
    r.retirement_type,
    r.lap AS retirement_lap,
    r.position_order AS retirement_position_order,
    r.status_id AS retirement_status_id,
    res.result_id,
    res.position AS result_position,
    res.position_text AS result_position_text,
    res.status_id AS result_status_id,
    sr.result_id AS sprint_result_id,
    sr.position AS sprint_position,
    sr.position_text AS sprint_position_text,
    sr.status_id AS sprint_status_id
  FROM lap_positions lp
  LEFT JOIN lap_positions lp_prev
    ON lp.race_id = lp_prev.race_id
    AND lp.driver_id = lp_prev.driver_id
    AND lp_prev.lap = lp.lap - 1
  LEFT JOIN pit_stops ps
    ON lp.race_id = ps.race_id
    AND lp.driver_id = ps.driver_id
    AND ps.lap IN (lp.lap, lp.lap - 1)
  LEFT JOIN retirements r
    ON lp.race_id = r.race_id
    AND lp.driver_id = r.driver_id
  LEFT JOIN results res
    ON lp.race_id = res.race_id
    AND lp.driver_id = res.driver_id
  LEFT JOIN sprint_results sr
    ON lp.race_id = sr.race_id
    AND lp.driver_id = sr.driver_id
  WHERE lp.lap IS NOT NULL
    AND lp.position IS NOT NULL
    AND (lp.lap = 1 OR lp_prev.lap IS NOT NULL)
    AND (
      r.lap IS NOT NULL
      OR ps.lap IS NOT NULL
      OR lp_prev.lap IS NOT NULL
    )
)
SELECT
  overtake_type,
  COUNT(*) AS count
FROM (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN cv.retirement_lap = cv.lap THEN 'R'
      WHEN cv.pit_lap = cv.lap THEN 'P'
      WHEN cv.pit_lap = cv.prev_lap THEN 'P'
      ELSE 'O'
    END AS overtake_type
  FROM chunk_view_0 cv
  JOIN races_ext re ON cv.race_id = re.race_id
  WHERE re.is_pit_data_available IS NOT NULL
    AND re.is_pit_data_available <> '0'
) t
GROUP BY overtake_type

rows.question: What is the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations, considering only the leaf-level items within each combination after fully expanding any nested packaging relationships?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH chunk_view_0 AS (
SELECT
  p.id AS packaging_id,
  p.name AS packaging_name,
  pr.contains_id AS child_packaging_id,
  pr.qty AS child_qty
FROM packaging p
LEFT JOIN packaging_relations pr
  ON p.id = pr.packaging_id
)
SELECT AVG(total_qty) AS average_total_quantity_across_final_packaging_combinations
FROM (
  WITH RECURSIVE
  -- roots: packaging that are not contained by any other packaging (final combinations)
  roots(root_id) AS (
    SELECT p.id
    FROM packaging p
    WHERE p.id NOT IN (SELECT contains_id FROM packaging_relations)
  ),
  -- recursive expansion: track current node, cumulative multiplier from root to current
  expand(root_id, node_id, cumulative_qty) AS (
    -- start from each root: find its direct children; if no children, it might be a leaf itself handled below
    SELECT r.root_id, pr.contains_id, pr.qty * 1.0
    FROM roots r
    JOIN packaging_relations pr ON pr.packaging_id = r.root_id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT e.root_id, pr.contains_id, e.cumulative_qty * pr.qty
    FROM expand e
    JOIN packaging_relations pr ON pr.packaging_id = e.node_id
  ),
  -- identify leaves: nodes that do not act as a parent in packaging_relations
  leaves AS (
    -- leaves that were reached via expansion
    SELECT e.root_id, e.node_id AS leaf_id, e.cumulative_qty
    FROM expand e
    WHERE e.node_id NOT IN (SELECT packaging_id FROM packaging_relations)
    UNION
    -- handle roots that have no children at all: they are leaf-level items themselves
    SELECT r.root_id, r.root_id AS leaf_id, 1.0 AS cumulative_qty
    FROM roots r
    WHERE r.root_id NOT IN (SELECT packaging_id FROM packaging_relations)
  ),
  -- sum per-root the total quantity of leaf-level items (using cumulative multipliers)
  per_root_totals AS (
    SELECT l.root_id, SUM(l.cumulative_qty) AS total_qty
    FROM leaves l
    GROUP BY l.root_id
    HAVING SUM(l.cumulative_qty) > 0
  )
  SELECT total_qty FROM per_root_totals
)

rows.question: Which customer has the highest average monthly change in payment amounts? Provide the customer's full name.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH chunk_view_0 AS (
SELECT
  p.payment_id,
  p.customer_id,
  p.amount,
  p.payment_date,
  p.last_update
FROM payment p
)
SELECT
  c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_full_name,
  avg_changes.avg_monthly_change
FROM customer c
JOIN (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    AVG(change) AS avg_monthly_change,
    COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', payment_date)) AS months_count
  FROM (
    SELECT
      p.*,
      ABS(p.amount - LAG(p.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY p.customer_id ORDER BY p.payment_date, p.payment_id)) AS change
    FROM payment p
  ) diffs
  WHERE change IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING months_count >= 2
) avg_changes USING (customer_id)
ORDER BY avg_changes.avg_monthly_change DESC
LIMIT 1

rows.question: In the United States, for Q4 2019 and Q4 2020, first select only those cities where total sales (with no promotions) rose by at least 20% from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020. Among these cities, rank products by their overall sales (still excluding promotions) in those quarters and take the top 20%. Then compute each top product’s share of total sales in Q4 2019 and Q4 2020 and calculate the difference in share from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020, returning the results in descending order of that share change.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT
    cu.cust_city,
    sa.prod_id,
    t.calendar_year,
    SUM(sa.amount_sold) AS amt
  FROM sales sa
  JOIN times t ON sa.time_id = t.time_id
  JOIN customers cu ON sa.cust_id = cu.cust_id
  JOIN countries co ON cu.country_id = co.country_id
  WHERE co.country_name = 'United States of Ame'  -- match actual column name
    AND t.calendar_quarter_number = 4
    AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
    AND sa.promo_id IS NULL
  GROUP BY cu.cust_city, sa.prod_id, t.calendar_year
),
city_prod_sums AS (
  SELECT
    cust_city,
    prod_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2019 THEN amt ELSE 0 END) AS sales_q4_2019,
    SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2020 THEN amt ELSE 0 END) AS sales_q4_2020,
    SUM(amt) AS combined_sum
  FROM raw
  GROUP BY cust_city, prod_id
),
city_totals AS (
  SELECT
    cust_city,
    SUM(sales_q4_2019) AS city_total_q4_2019,
    SUM(sales_q4_2020) AS city_total_q4_2020
  FROM city_prod_sums
  GROUP BY cust_city
),
eligible_cities AS (
  SELECT cust_city
  FROM city_totals
  WHERE city_total_q4_2019 IS NOT NULL
    AND city_total_q4_2019 > 0
    AND city_total_q4_2020 >= 1.20 * city_total_q4_2019
),
top_products_per_city AS (
  SELECT cust_city, prod_id
  FROM (
    SELECT
      cps.cust_city,
      cps.prod_id,
      cps.combined_sum,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cps.cust_city ORDER BY cps.combined_sum DESC) AS rn,
      COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY cps.cust_city) AS cnt
    FROM city_prod_sums cps
    JOIN eligible_cities ec ON cps.cust_city = ec.cust_city
  )
  WHERE rn <= CASE
      WHEN cnt <= 5 THEN 1
      ELSE CAST( (cnt * 0.20) AS INTEGER )
    END
),
final_data AS (
  SELECT
    cps.cust_city,
    p.prod_name,
    cps.sales_q4_2019,
    cps.sales_q4_2020,
    ct.city_total_q4_2019,
    ct.city_total_q4_2020
  FROM city_prod_sums cps
  JOIN top_products_per_city tp ON cps.cust_city = tp.cust_city AND cps.prod_id = tp.prod_id
  JOIN city_totals ct ON cps.cust_city = ct.cust_city
  LEFT JOIN products p ON cps.prod_id = p.prod_id
)
SELECT
  cust_city AS city,
  prod_name AS product,
  COALESCE(sales_q4_2019, 0.0) AS sales_q4_2019,
  COALESCE(sales_q4_2020, 0.0) AS sales_q4_2020,
  city_total_q4_2019,
  city_total_q4_2020,
  CASE WHEN city_total_q4_2019 = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE COALESCE(sales_q4_2019,0.0) / city_total_q4_2019 END AS share_q4_2019,
  CASE WHEN city_total_q4_2020 = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE COALESCE(sales_q4_2020,0.0) / city_total_q4_2020 END AS share_q4_2020,
  (CASE WHEN city_total_q4_2020 = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE COALESCE(sales_q4_2020,0.0) / city_total_q4_2020 END)
    - (CASE WHEN city_total_q4_2019 = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE COALESCE(sales_q4_2019,0.0) / city_total_q4_2019 END)
    AS share_change
FROM final_data
ORDER BY share_change DESC

rows.question: For each year, calculate the percentage of films that had exclusively female actors (meaning no male actors and no actors with unknown/unspecified gender). Consider actors with gender marked as 'Male' or 'None' as non-female. For the results, display the year, the total number of movies in that year, and the percentage of movies with exclusively female actors. Extract the year from the Movie.year field by taking the last 4 characters and converting to a number.

  Movie.MID,
  Movie.year,
  Movie.title,
  Person.PID,

rows.question: How did each salesperson's annual total sales compare to their annual sales quota? Provide the difference between their total sales and the quota for each year, organized by salesperson and year.

rows.question: Calculate the duration of each track, classify them as short, medium, or long, output the minimum and maximum time for each kind (in minutes) and the total revenue for each category, group by the category.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH track_stats AS (
  SELECT
    t.TrackId,
    t.Milliseconds,
    CAST(t.Milliseconds AS REAL) / 60000.0 AS duration_minutes
  FROM "Track" t
),
overall AS (
  SELECT
    MIN(duration_minutes) AS min_d,
    AVG(duration_minutes) AS avg_d,
    MAX(duration_minutes) AS max_d
  FROM track_stats
),
boundaries AS (
  SELECT
    min_d,
    avg_d,
    max_d,
    (min_d + avg_d) / 2.0 AS mid_min_avg,
    (avg_d + max_d) / 2.0 AS mid_avg_max
  FROM overall
),
track_with_category AS (
  SELECT
    ts.TrackId,
    ts.duration_minutes,
    CASE
      WHEN ts.duration_minutes >= b.min_d AND ts.duration_minutes <= b.mid_min_avg THEN 'Short'
      WHEN ts.duration_minutes > b.mid_min_avg AND ts.duration_minutes <= b.mid_avg_max THEN 'Medium'
      WHEN ts.duration_minutes > b.mid_avg_max AND ts.duration_minutes <= b.max_d THEN 'Long'
      ELSE 'Unknown'
    END AS category
  FROM track_stats ts
  CROSS JOIN boundaries b
),
track_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    il.TrackId,
    SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS revenue
  FROM "InvoiceLine" il
  GROUP BY il.TrackId
)
SELECT
  twc.category AS category,
  MIN(twc.duration_minutes) AS category_min_minutes,
  MAX(twc.duration_minutes) AS category_max_minutes,
  SUM(COALESCE(tr.revenue, 0.0)) AS category_total_revenue
FROM track_with_category twc
LEFT JOIN track_revenue tr ON tr.TrackId = twc.TrackId
GROUP BY twc.category
ORDER BY
  CASE twc.category WHEN 'Short' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'Long' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END
